questions.q: Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{10}$ be a G.P. If $\frac{a_{3}}{a_{1}}=25,$ then $\frac{a_{9}}{a_{5}}$ equals :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $a_{1}=a, a_{2}=a r, a_{3}=a r^{2} \ldots a_{10}=a r^{9}$

where $r=$ common ratio of given G.P.

Given, $\frac{a_{3}}{a_{1}}=25\Rightarrow \frac{a r^{2}}{a}=25\Rightarrow r=\pm 5$

Now, $\frac{a_{9}}{a_{5}}=\frac{a r^{8}}{a r^{4}}=r^{4}=(\pm 5)^{4}=5^{4}$

We know that,

Total number of three digit number will be 999-99=900,

Now,

Number of 3- digit number which are divisible by 3 will be 9003=300,

Number of 3- digit number which are divisible by 4 will be 9004=225,

Number of 3- digit number which are divisible by 3 & 4 both will be 90012=75,

So , number of 3- digit number which are divisible by 3 or 4 will be 300+225-75=450,

Now, number of 3- digit number which are divisible by 48 is 90048=18

So, number of 3- digit number which are divisible by 3 or 4 but not 48 will be 

=450-18=432

Let the $\mathrm{I}^{\text {st }}$ term of G.P. be a \& common ratio be r
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{a}_3 \mathrm{a}_5 & =\operatorname{ar}^2 \cdot \operatorname{ar}^4=729 \\ & =\mathrm{a}^2 \mathrm{r}^6=729 \\ & =\mathrm{ar}^3=27 \quad ....(i)
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{a}_2+\mathrm{a}_4 & =\mathrm{ar}+\mathrm{ar}^3=\frac{111}{4} \\ & =\mathrm{ar}=\frac{3}{4} \quad ....(ii)\end{aligned}$
$\text { (i) } \div \text { (ii) }$
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{ar}^3}{\mathrm{ar}}=\frac{27}{3 / 4} \\ & \mathrm{r}^2=36 \\ & \mathrm{r}=6
\end{aligned}$
from (ii)
$a(6)=\frac{3}{4} \Rightarrow a=\frac{1}{8}$
Now, $24\left(a_1+a_2+a_3\right)$
$\begin{aligned}
& =24\left(a+a r+a^2\right) \\ & =24 a\left(1+r+r^2\right)
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & =24 \times \frac{1}{8}(1+6+36) \\ & =3(43) \\ & =129\end{aligned}$

Multiply x-y both sides

⇒x-yS=x-y(x+y+x2+xy+y2+x3+x2y+xy2+y3+...)

⇒x-yS=x-yx+y+x-yx2+xy+y2+x-yx3+x2y+xy2+y3+.....

⇒x-yS=x2-y2+x3-y3+x4-y4+.....

⇒x-yS=x2+x3+x4+....-y2+y3+y4+.....

S=1x-yx21-x-y21-y=1x-yx2-x2y-y2+xy2(1-x)(1-y)

S=x+y-xy(1-x)(1-y)

questions.q: $\text { In an arithmetic progression, if } S_{40}=1030 \text { and } S_{12}=57 \text {, then } S_{30}-S_{10} \text { is equal to : }$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& S_{40}=1030 \Rightarrow \frac{40}{2}[2 a+39 d]=1030 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 a+39 d=\frac{103}{2}....(1) \\
& \quad S_{12}=57 \Rightarrow \frac{12}{2}[2 a+11 d]=57 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 a+11 d=\frac{57}{6}...(2)
\end{aligned}$
Equation (1) - equation (2)
$\begin{aligned}
& 28 d=\frac{103}{2}-\frac{57}{6} \\
& 28 d=\frac{309-57}{6}
\end{aligned}d=\frac{3}{2}\Rightarrow \quad a=-\frac{7}{2}S_{30}-S_{10}=\frac{30}{2}[2 a+29 d]-\frac{10}{2}[2 a+9 d]=15[2 a+29 d]-5[2 a+9 d]=5[6 a+87 d-2 a-9 d]=5[4 a+78 d]=5[-14+117]=515$

Let the sum of its <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>6</mn><mtext>th </mtext></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>8</mn><mtext>th </mtext></msup></math> terms be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> and the product of its <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>3</mn><mtext>rd </mtext></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>5</mn><mtext>th </mtext></msup></math> terms be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></math>. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

a1,a2,a3,…. be a G.P. of increasing positive numbers,

And the sum of its 6th  and 8th  terms be 2

So, a6+a8=2

⇒ar5+ar7=2  .....1

And the product of its 3rd  and 5th  terms be 19,

So, a3·a5=19⇒a2·r2·r4=19

⇒ar3=13

Now from putting the value of ar3=13 in equation 1 we get,

r23+r43=2

⇒r4+r2=6

⇒r2+3r2-2=0

⇒r2=2

ar3=13⇒ar·2=13⇒ar=16

Now finding the value of 6a2+a4a4+a6, we get

=6ar+ar3ar3+ar5

=616+1313+23

=6·12·1=3

questions.q: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>…</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo></math> are A.P. and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>10</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>10</mn></msub><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>10</mn></msub></math> then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> is equal to

questions.solution:
Given, a1,a2,a3......& b1,b2,b3.....are in A.P

Also given, a1=2, a10=3

and a1b1=1=a10b10

So b1=1a1=12 and b10=1a10=13

Now using nth term formula we get, a10=a1+9da⇒3=2+9da

⇒da=19

Using same formula we get,

 b10=b1+9db ⇒13=12+9db ⇒db=-154

Now calculating a4b4=a1+3dab1+3db

=2+3×1912+3×-154

= 73×818=5654=2827

questions.q:
Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ be in an arithmetic progression of positive terms.
Let $\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{k}}=\mathrm{a}_1^2-\mathrm{a}_2^2+\mathrm{a}_3^2-\mathrm{a}_4^2+\ldots+\mathrm{a}_{2 \mathrm{k}-1}^2-\mathrm{a}_{2 \mathrm{k}}^2$.
If $\mathrm{A}_3=-153, \mathrm{~A}_5=-435$ and $\mathrm{a}_1^2+\mathrm{a}_2^2+\mathrm{a}_3^2=66$, then $\mathrm{a}_{17}-\mathrm{A}_7$ is equal to______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{d} \rightarrow \text { common diff. } \\ & \mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{k}}=-\mathrm{kd}[2 \mathrm{a}+(2 \mathrm{k}-1) \mathrm{d}] \\ & \mathrm{A}_3=-153 \\ & \Rightarrow 153=13 \mathrm{~d}[2 \mathrm{a}+5 \mathrm{~d}] \\ & 51=\mathrm{d}[2 \mathrm{a}+5 \mathrm{~d}]...(1) \\ & \mathrm{A}_5=-435 \\ & 435=5 \mathrm{~d}[2 \mathrm{a}+9 \mathrm{~d}] \\ & 87=\mathrm{d}[2 \mathrm{a}+9 \mathrm{~d}] \\ & (2)-(1) \\ & 36=4 \mathrm{~d}^2 \\ & \mathrm{~d}=3, \mathrm{a}=1 \\ & \mathrm{a}_{17}-\mathrm{A}_7=49-[-7.3[2+39]]=910\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Since, a,b,118 are in GP, so

a18=b2

⇒a=18b2   ....1

Also, 1a,10,1 b are in A.P., so

1a+1b=20

⇒a+b=20ab

⇒18b2+b=360b3

⇒360b2-18b-1=0    ∵  b≠0

⇒b=18±324+1440720

⇒  b=18+1764720    ∵ b>0

If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mi>z</mi></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><msup><mo>)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that 1x,1y,1z are in AP and x,2y,z are in GP.

As given, 2y=1x+1y .......i
Also, 2y2=xz .......ii

Also given that xy+yz+zx=32xyz
⇒1x+1y+1z=32 .....iii
From (i) and (iii) we get 3y=32

y=2 .....iv

Now from (ii) xz=4  .......v

Now using (ii), (iv) and (v)

⇒x+z=42

Hence 3(x+y+z)2=3(2+42)2

=150

Therefore, this is the required answer.
